main_issue: How to handle D's strong-smelling sambal belacan cooking in the shared kitchen: A wants it restricted, B and C favour a window fan, D wants to keep cooking it.

A-B.evidence: B proposes the fan (6, 12, 20); A says a fan won't be enough (11) and settles on timing with D (15-17); B says the timing doesn't fix room and laundry (18), so they partly agree the smell is a problem but not on the remedy.

A-C.evidence: C backs the fan (9, 13, 21), A doubts it (11); both object to the smell, and C says the laundry is still affected after the timing deal (19).

A-D.evidence: A asks for no strong-smelling cooking (1) and D protests (4, 14); A then proposes weekends or after 7 p.m. (15), and D agrees: 'Okay. After 7... I can do that' (16), A thanks D (17).

B-C.evidence: C objects to blowing the smell toward the yard (7), B concedes and redirects the fan out the window (8), C agrees (9), and both keep pushing the fan (12-13, 20-21).

B-D.evidence: B proposes the fan (6); D doubts it will help and objects to setting one up each time (10, 14); D accepts the timing rule (16), which B says is insufficient (18).

C-D.evidence: C backs the fan (9, 13, 21) while D is skeptical (10, 14); C says the timing deal leaves the laundry affected (19).
